title_original: Glenn Close Says Her ‘Career Is to Create Characters For Gay Halloween Parades’

blocks.text: Glenn Close is leaning into the campy side of her work.
The legendary actress joked with me Sunday night on the red carpet at the Governors Awards in Hollywood that so much of her career has been for her LGBTQ fans.
“My career is to create characters for gay Halloween parades,” she said, smiling.

blocks.caption: Glenn Close accepts the Honorary Oscar Award onstage at the 17th Governors Awards held at The Ray Dolby Ballroom at Ovation Hollywood on November 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Variety via Getty Images

blocks.text: Close’s latest addition to her gay Halloween parade collection is Drusilla Sickle in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.” Her outlandish look, which she designed, is sure to be popular next Halloween. “It’s one of the characters like Cruella, like Norma Desmond, the character isn’t there until you’re in full drag,” she said. “It’s really fun.”

blocks.alt: L to R: Anne Hathaway is Penelope and Tom Holland is Telemachus in THE ODYSSEY, written, produced, and directed by Christopher Nolan.

blocks.text: She joked she didn’t need an honorary Oscar because there’s “nothing better” than being impersonated by gay fans at Halloween parades.

Close received an honorary Oscar at the 17 th Governors Awards after being nominated eight times for acting Academy Awards without winning. She wants to have her freshly minted Oscar displayed at the local library near her home in Montana. “So people can actually see what an Oscar looks like,” she said.

blocks.caption: Marc Albu, Annie Starke and Glenn Close at the 17th Governors Awards held at The Ray Dolby Ballroom at Ovation Hollywood on November 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Variety via Getty Images

blocks.text: In addition to Close, Ridley Scott and Disney’s first Black animator Floyd Norman also received honorary Oscars. Scott previously announced that he was unable to make it to Los Angles to accept the award in person.
Killer Films co-founders Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler will receive the Irving G. Thalberg, making the, the first female producing team and first independent producers to earn the honor.
“The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” is in theaters Nov. 20.
